draft.definition: סְדֹם names the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם means “the king of Sodom.” The place name identifies the city ruled by the king who speaks to Abram.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם אֶל אַבְרָם, the king of Sodom speaks, and אֶל introduces Abram as the person he addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם אֶל אַבְרָם, the king of Sodom speaks to Abram. The preposition אֶל introduces the name of the person addressed.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: The king of Sodom says תֶּן לִי הַנֶּפֶשׁ, “Give me the people.” לִי identifies the king as the recipient, and הַנֶּפֶשׁ collectively designates the people. The parallel command קַח לָךְ tells Abram to take the goods for himself.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram.

analysis.evidence: The king of Sodom asks Abram to give him הַנֶּפֶשׁ and to take הָרְכֻשׁ, the possessions, for himself. The two requests distinguish the recovered people from their goods.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial נ of the absolute singular noun נֶפֶשׁ, tagged for both genders. The singular refers collectively to the people.

draft.change: Add the root רכש and its noun רְכוּשׁ for acquired possessions. The source’s personal-name gloss does not fit this occurrence.
draft.definition: Property or goods that someone owns, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:5 pairs רְכוּשָׁם, “their possessions,” with רָכָשׁוּ, “they had acquired.”

analysis.evidence: The king of Sodom tells Abram to give him the people (תֶּן לִי הַנֶּפֶשׁ) and to take the goods for himself (וְהָרְכֻשׁ קַח לָךְ). The contrast identifies רְכֻשׁ as property in general.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ and the definite article הָ precede a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.
